description: Property-based amino acid substitution strategies for TCR-pMHC mutation design

property_based_rules.rationale: Maintain hydrophobic core packing while tuning sidechain geometry and flexibility
when_to_use: Core interface positions with hydrophobic contacts

strategy_details.L_to_I: Adds beta-branching, increases rigidity, favors beta-sheets
strategy_details.L_to_V: Reduces size (~20% volume), maintains branching, increases rigidity
strategy_details.L_to_M: Adds flexibility via sulfur, similar volume, oxidation-sensitive
strategy_details.I_to_V: Reduces size, maintains beta-branching and rigidity
strategy_details.V_to_L: Increases size and flexibility, better helix former
strategy_details.M_to_L: Removes sulfur flexibility, similar volume, more stable

examples.outcome: No change in affinity, increased flexibility

cautions: Check available space before increasing size (V→L, V→I)
M is oxidation-sensitive in some contexts
Beta-branched residues (I, V) are more rigid

property_based_rules.rationale: Tune pi-pi stacking strength, H-bonding capability, and sidechain volume
when_to_use: CDR3 hotspot positions with aromatic contacts

strategy_details.Y_to_F: Removes OH (H-bond donor/acceptor), reduces size by 4 Å³, pure hydrophobic aromatic
strategy_details.Y_to_W: Increases size by 34 Å³, adds indole NH (H-bond donor), strongest pi-stacking
strategy_details.F_to_Y: Adds OH (H-bond capability), increases polarity, slightly larger
strategy_details.F_to_W: Largest increase (38 Å³), adds H-bond donor, strongest pi-stacking, check steric clash
strategy_details.W_to_Y: Reduces size, maintains H-bond donor, loses indole NH
strategy_details.W_to_F: Largest reduction, removes all H-bonding, pure hydrophobic

examples.reason: Removed bulky OH, improved pi-pi stacking geometry

examples.context: CDR3β F97 near peptide acidic residue
examples.reason: Added H-bond capability to stabilize interaction

cautions: Y→W and F→W require checking for steric clashes (W is bulky)
Removing Y OH may break critical H-bonds
W is rare in CDR3 (only 2-3% frequency)
Check if aromatic partner is present (peptide F, Y, W, or charged residue for cation-pi)

property_based_rules.rationale: Maintain electrostatic interactions while optimizing salt bridge geometry
when_to_use: Optimizing reach to distant charged partner

strategy_details.R_to_K: Shortens sidechain by ~1 Å, monodentate vs bidentate H-bond, more flexible
strategy_details.K_to_R: Lengthens sidechain, adds bidentate H-bond capability, stronger interaction
strategy_details.E_to_D: Shortens sidechain by ~1 Å, more compact salt bridge
strategy_details.D_to_E: Lengthens sidechain, better for distant partners, more flexible

examples.context: CDR3β R155 salt bridge at 4.2 Å
examples.outcome: No improvement (distance too long for K)
examples.reason: K sidechain too short to reach partner

examples.context: CDR3α K96 salt bridge at 3.8 Å
examples.reason: R bidentate H-bond stronger than K monodentate

examples.context: CDR3α D92 salt bridge at 4.5 Å

cautions: Measure salt bridge distance first (use MD average)
R→K fails if distance > 4.0 Å
D→E may introduce flexibility (entropy penalty)
Check if partner is truly charged (HIS pKa ~6, may be neutral)

property_based_rules.rationale: Maintain H-bonding capability while tuning sidechain size and flexibility

strategy_details.S_to_T: Adds methyl group (beta-branching), increases rigidity, favors beta-sheets
strategy_details.N_to_Q: Extends sidechain by ~1 Å, better reach for H-bonds
strategy_details.Q_to_N: Shortens sidechain, more compact H-bond network

examples.context: CDR3α S94 H-bond to peptide backbone
examples.reason: T methyl group improved hydrophobic packing nearby
Q longer reach bridged the gap

cautions: S/T are phosphorylation sites (may affect regulation)
N/Q can deamidate over time (stability issue)
T beta-branching may clash in tight spaces

property_based_rules.rationale: Avoid steric clashes or voids by matching sidechain volume
when_to_use: Buried positions with low RMSF (< 1.5 Å)
Avoiding introduction of voids or clashes

strategy_details.one_group_up: Moderate risk, check for space (e.g., V→L)
strategy_details.one_group_down: May create void, check if flexibility compensates (e.g., L→V)

examples.reason: Created small void but no functional impact

cautions: Volume alone insufficient, also check shape (linear vs branched)
Flexible regions (RMSF > 3 Å) tolerate size changes better
Buried positions are less tolerant than surface positions

property_based_rules.rationale: Introduce or remove H-bond donors/acceptors to optimize interaction networks

examples.context: CDR3α L96 near peptide backbone carbonyl
examples.reason: S OH formed new H-bond to backbone

examples.context: CDR3β S100 with no H-bond partners

cautions: Buried polar groups without H-bond partners are destabilizing
H-bonds are directional (check geometry, not just distance)
Solvent-exposed H-bonds are weaker (compete with water)

forbidden_substitutions.reason: Breaks electrostatic interactions and introduces repulsion

examples.context: CDR3β R155 salt bridge to peptide E6

forbidden_substitutions.reason: Rigidifies backbone, breaks H-bonds, disrupts induced fit

examples.reason: P rigidified loop, prevented induced fit

forbidden_substitutions.reason: Glycine provides flexibility essential for tight backbone angles
Risk of aberrant disulfide bonds and aggregation

step_1_identify_interaction.description: Determine the type of interaction at the target position
questions: What is the partner residue? (peptide, MHC, or TCR)
What is the interaction type? (hydrophobic, pi-pi, salt bridge, H-bond)
What is the RRCS value? (>3.0 = strong hotspot)
What is the occupancy? (>70% = stable interaction)

step_2_check_properties.description: Analyze amino acid properties of current and partner residues
questions: What is the charge state? (positive, negative, neutral)
What is the size? (volume in Å³)
Does it have H-bond capability? (donor, acceptor, both, none)
Is it aromatic? (F, Y, W, H)

step_3_select_strategy.description: Choose substitution strategy based on interaction type

step_4_check_constraints.description: Verify substitution does not violate constraints
checks: Is it a forbidden substitution? (charge reversal, Pro in CDR3, etc.)
Is the size change acceptable? (within ±20% volume)
Is there space for larger sidechain? (check RMSF and local geometry)
Will it break critical H-bonds? (check H-bond network)
Is the region tolerant to mutation? (CDR3 > CDR1/2 > Framework)

metrics.stability_change: Core mutations risk destabilization, surface mutations safer

cdr3_aromatic_hotspot.description: Optimize aromatic hotspots in CDR3 loops
best_practices: Target positions with RRCS > 3.0 and occupancy > 70%
Try Y→F first (removes OH, often improves geometry)
Try F→Y if H-bond partner is present
Avoid Y→W or F→W unless space is confirmed (check RMSF > 3 Å)
Check for pi-pi stacking partner (aromatic or charged residue)
Measure salt bridge distance from MD (average over trajectory)
If distance > 4.0 Å: try D→E or K→R (lengthen)
If distance < 3.0 Å: try E→D or R→K (shorten)
If distance 3.0-4.0 Å: try K→R (bidentate H-bond)
Target buried positions with low RMSF (< 2 Å)
Consider beta-branching (I, V) for tighter packing
Avoid introducing polar residues in hydrophobic cores
